title: The Extent to Which
gist_ar: نص فني متخصص عن تحديد المعايير: الرقم الواحد اللي بيلخّص كل حاجة بيخفي أكتر مما يوضح.
text:
The index, most of whom who cite it have never examined, combines nine
indicators, many of which measure the same underlying quantity. This note
delineates what it can and cannot support.

Begin with the parameters. Each indicator is normalised to a scale of one to
ten, a step by means of which incommensurable quantities are made addable, and at
which point most of the interpretive damage is done. Air quality, a continuous
variable with a well-characterised threshold above which harm is documented, is
thereby rendered comparable to institutional trust, for which no threshold has
ever been specified. The way in which the two are then averaged implies a
spectrum of equivalent magnitude. There is none.

Two consequences follow, as a result of which the index is routinely
misapplied. First, movement is uninterpretable at the margin: a city may rise
four places on changes in three indicators, none of which is individually
significant, in which case the aggregate is precise without being accurate.
Second, the criterion by which cities are grouped into bands is a quantile, not a
substantive cut, whereby a difference of 0.2 becomes a difference of category.

The index does one thing well, and it is worth being explicit about it. Where the
degree to which two cities differ is large — a point at which the composite
comfortably exceeds its own error — the ranking is robust and has been validated
against nuanced local data on four occasions.

Used comprehensively, it is a screening instrument. Used to quantify improvement
year on year, it characterises noise. The distinction is not subtle, and the
elaborate methodological appendix, which does specify it, is not what gets read.

questions.q: What does the writer say the index is genuinely good for?
options: Comparing cities that differ by a wide margin
Measuring year-on-year improvement, which it does more reliably than wide comparisons

questions.q: What is the problem with normalising to a one-to-ten scale?
questions.q_ar: إيه مشكلة التوحيد على مقياس من واحد لعشرة؟
options: It makes incommensurable quantities addable and implies equivalent magnitude

questions.q: Why is movement at the margin uninterpretable?
questions.q_ar: ليه الحركة عند الحدود مش قابلة للتفسير؟
options: A city can move several places on changes none of which is individually significant

questions.q: What does the writer note about the methodological appendix?
options: It does specify the limitation, and is not what gets read
It contradicts the index's own rankings and recommends the composite be abandoned
